svg.title: Adaptive bits: mixed-precision allocation at 48 bytes
svg.desc: Animated bar chart of how a 48-byte budget is spread over 384 principal components of SciFact's bge-small embeddings. Uniform binary gives every component 1 bit (recall@10 0.611). Variance-based allocation concentrates bits on the leading components and gives 97 components none (0.694); query-weighted allocation goes further, 158 components with none (0.703).
svg.text: Adaptive bits: the same 48 bytes, spent where they matter
variance per principal component, relative to the first (log scale, clipped at 0.001)
bits per group of 8 components (48 bytes = 384 bits in all)
Uniform: 1 bit on every dimension (binary, 48 B)
mixed48-pca: rotate to principal components, spend bits where the variance is
mixed48-pca-w: weight variance by how much energy queries put there
recall@10 without re-scoring: 0.611 · components with 0 bits: 0 of 384
recall@10 without re-scoring: 0.694 · components with 0 bits: 97 of 384
recall@10 without re-scoring: 0.703 · components with 0 bits: 158 of 384
bits return to the last 44 components: little variance,
but 28% of the corpus mean, which every query points along
Real data: SciFact, bge-small-en-v1.5, 8,036 chunks, 300 claims. pq48 at the same 48 bytes reaches 0.711.
Mixed precision by importance is the idea behind structure-aware MoE quantization (QuantMoE-Bench).
